To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we can rewrite xpath queries to sql queries by means of an lfp operator, (ii) we can translate xpath queries to extended xpath expressions, and (iii) we can translate extended xpath expressions to a sequence of sql queries.

1) extended xpath expressions are a simple and powerful extension of xpath that can be translated into sql queries using only the lfp operator; 2) extended xpath expressions can be used to capture the semantics of xpath queries in the presence of dtds; 3) extended xpath expressions and their translations can be used for query rewriting in the presence of xml views.

we have developed a new approach to translate xpath queries into sql, and we have developed a complete framework to answer xpath queries over dtd-structured xml data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of answering xpath queries over xml views can be reduced to a sequence of sql queries.
the problem of answering xpath queries over xml stored in an rbdms can be addressed in a practical way by means of simple rdbms extensions.
the combination of xpath and dtds can be efficiently handled in rdbms, and that the lfp operator is a powerful tool to answer xpath queries over xml views of xml documents.
